To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the REALM-Short Form was a valid, reliable, easy to administer, and acceptable measure of English reading ability among patients with coronary heart disease in the UK.

the use of a validated health literacy screening tool, the Rapid Estimate of Adult Literacy in Medicine (REALM), in a UK population of people with CHD, identified that 1 in 5 had limited health literacy and that this group had poorer health behaviours and knowledge.
the REALM-SF is an effective tool for measuring health literacy in the UK population with coronary disease and that the REALM-50 and REALM-30 are less accurate.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relationship between health literacy and the quality of health care.
the following questions.

the relationship between literacy, numeracy and health literacy, the impact of health literacy on health outcomes and the impact of interventions designed to improve the health literacy of patients with chronic disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the REALM is not an adequate instrument to screen for low health literacy.
the use of the REALM in clinical practice is limited.
the REALM is a valid and reliable screening tool to measure health literacy in the UK population with coronary disease.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have demonstrated the feasibility of a new approach to the design of a screening tool that is based on a combination of qualitative and quantitative methods.
we have shown that the use of the REALM is a feasible method to assess health literacy in a UK population.
the results from the REALM-50 were comparable to those of the REALM.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the REALM-SF is a reliable and valid screening tool to measure health literacy in a UK population.
we need to be able to measure health literacy in a way that is valid, reliable, and responsive to change in order to be able to use it in clinical and public health practice.
we need to be able to assess the health literacy of the people we serve, so that we can tailor our messages to their level.
